methodological_rigor.justification: This is a registered prospective single-arm phase II trial (NCT04278092) with pre-specified primary endpoint (ORR at 12 weeks), formal sample size calculation based on one-sided exact binomial test, and ITT analysis. CONSORT flow diagram is included. The study is well-conducted for a single-arm design in an indication without established standard of care. Key limitations include the single-arm design without a randomized comparator, small sample (n=57), and reliance on historical controls from different treatment contexts (pre-immunotherapy era). The post hoc subgroup analyses by prior therapy type are hypothesis-generating only.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is the first prospective trial specifically addressing the post-immunotherapy evidence gap in R/M SCCHN, an area where no standard of care exists. An ORR of 43.9% exceeding the 10% null hypothesis threshold and median OS of 12.2 months substantially above historical pre-immunotherapy benchmarks (OS ~5-7 months) is clinically meaningful. The inclusion of ECOG PS 2 patients enhances real-world generalizability. The findings provide the highest-quality prospective evidence available for this clinical scenario and directly support PTX+C as a practical second-line option.

reporting_quality.justification: CONSORT reporting is well adhered to: flow diagram, eligibility criteria, protocol amendment disclosure, primary and secondary endpoints pre-specified, safety grading by CTCAE, and QoL analyses including sensitivity analyses with missing data imputation. The transparent reporting of the protocol amendment and the platinum-resistant patient deviation is commendable. Supplementary materials are redacted. No data sharing statement is present.

novelty_literature.justification: PaceAce is the first prospective trial specifically designed for PTX+C after first-line pembrolizumab failure in R/M SCCHN—a clinically critical and understudied setting. Prior data were limited to retrospective series with heterogeneous populations and regimens. The study fills a clearly documented evidence gap with a homogeneous, carefully defined patient population (all CPS ≥1, no prior cetuximab, post-first-line pembrolizumab only). The QoL component and the exploratory OS from first-line start add further originality.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is clearly written with logical organization and appropriate contextualization of results within the limited prior literature. Limitations are specifically articulated, including the potential null hypothesis mismatch with the mixed platinum-sensitivity population. Safety data are transparently reported including fatal AEs. The discussion appropriately distinguishes between the prospective study findings and exploratory subgroup analyses.

key_strengths: First prospective trial specifically targeting post-pembrolizumab R/M SCCHN with a homogeneous, well-defined patient population and pre-registered design
ORR of 43.9% greatly exceeds the 10% null hypothesis and historical benchmarks, with median OS of 12.2 months versus 5-7 months historical controls
QoL assessment with EORTC QLQ-C30 and H&N35 including sensitivity analyses for missing data adds clinical completeness
Inclusion of ECOG PS 2 patients (7%) enhances real-world applicability beyond typical trial populations
key_concerns: Single-arm design without randomized comparator precludes definitive conclusions about relative efficacy; ORR from historical controls (pre-immunotherapy era) may underestimate expected responses in immunotherapy-naive context
Small sample (n=57) limits statistical power for secondary and exploratory subgroup analyses
Sepsis incidence of 10.5% with two fatal cases despite low febrile neutropenia rate warrants attention to G-CSF prophylaxis recommendations
Null hypothesis ORR of 10% from pre-immunotherapy settings may not be appropriate for this post-pembrolizumab population, potentially making the primary endpoint easier to achieve
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-conducted first prospective trial in an important clinical gap with compelling efficacy results; it qualifies for Tier 2 as the first prospective evidence base for a practical post-immunotherapy regimen in R/M SCCHN, with minor revisions needed to address the null hypothesis rationale and G-CSF prophylaxis guidance.
